finding.problem: The line qualifies its assertion as biological autonomy, but the endpoint has an exclusively managerial definition. A reader following the line can infer that self-production explains operational discretion even though the scope note denies that inference.
finding.preferred_repair: Keep existing entry IDs and counts. Make the line an explicitly editorial distinction, and add reciprocal scope notes to the existing two profiles. A separate biological-autonomy node is unnecessary for this reader need.
rejected_shortcuts: Do not rename managerial autonomy to encompass all senses without developing them.
Do not infer that the biological theory grants staff decision rights.
Do not add a new node merely to change a coverage count.
Do not convert the distinction into historical influence.

edge_updates.plain_phrase: uses self-production in a sense distinct from the operational discretion described by
edge_updates.scope_conditions: The 1974 biological account concerns maintaining the organisation constituting a unity. The target entry concerns operational discretion within wider constraints. This is an editorial distinction between those uses, not a derivation of management rights from self-production.
edge_updates.inference_method: Editorial comparison of separately located biological and management accounts
edge_updates.source_locator: Varela, Maturana, and Uribe, sections 3–4, printed p. 188; Taylor, 10 May 2025 lecture, PDF p. 8 (bounded discretion) and p. 55 (autonomy and cohesion)
edge_updates.public_review_label: Editorial distinction; neither equivalence nor historical influence asserted
edge_updates.provenance_instruction: Preserve the prior record in the new release original-record ledger. Retain the existing edge ID so saved links remain valid; current provenance is not silently erased.

claim_updates.statement: The 1974 biological account concerns maintaining the organisation constituting a unity. The target entry concerns operational discretion within wider constraints. This is an editorial distinction between those uses, not a derivation of management rights from self-production.
claim_updates.notes: Editorial distinction; preserve both senses and their units of analysis. No theory of management autonomy is derived from the biological source.

evidence_additions.excerpt_or_summary: The authors explain autonomy through the continued operation of the organisation constituting a unity, including component production.
Taylor's teaching account places freedom to act within boundaries and balances organisational autonomy with cohesion.

profile_updates.append_to_summary: The paper's biological use of autonomy concerns self-production of a unity. It doesn't establish the decision rights of its parts.
append_open_checks: Any organisational application must state its components, production processes, unit of analysis, and decision rights separately.

profile_updates.append_to_summary: This entry concerns operational discretion within wider constraints. A claim about biological self-production neither assigns that discretion nor shows who may decide what.
append_open_checks: Do not infer delegated authority from an account of self-production.

source_rechecks.read_scope: Sections 3–4 and the six-part identification key in section 9; not the algorithm appendix or a model reproduction.
Title/date, bounded discretion on PDF p. 8, and autonomy/cohesion on PDF p. 55; not all 224 pages.
The distinction among operational, channel, and transducer capacity, and the limitations discussion.

counterexamples.status: Constructed editorial stress test; not an empirical case
counterexamples.scenario: A referral reaches the receiving team with every relevant distinction intact. The team can understand it but may authorise none of the responses it requires.
counterexamples.inference_that_fails: Adequate communication/transduction capacity establishes effective action.
counterexamples.reader_check: Identify the available actions, resources, and authority after the signal arrives.
counterexamples.basis: Beer, PDF pp. 6–8, distinguishes capacities; Taylor, PDF p. 8, makes freedom to act part of the work account. The referral itself is invented.

counterexamples.status: Constructed editorial stress test; not an empirical case
counterexamples.scenario: An analyst draws a durable box around an externally maintained machine and calls its continued operation self-production.
counterexamples.inference_that_fails: A stable boundary, repeated operation, or survival alone meets the autopoiesis criteria.
counterexamples.reader_check: Specify which processes produce the components and boundary, and whether they belong to the unity being described.
counterexamples.basis: Varela, Maturana, and Uribe, section 9, printed pp. 192–193. The machine is invented.

counterexamples.status: Constructed logical scope test; not an empirical claim
counterexamples.scenario: A claim about how a unity maintains itself is used to conclude that a particular organisational part should be free to choose its work.
counterexamples.inference_that_fails: A property asserted of the unity supplies a decision-rights arrangement for its parts.
counterexamples.reader_check: Keep the unit of analysis and the meaning of autonomy explicit at both endpoints.
counterexamples.basis: Comparison of the biological account on printed p. 188 with Taylor PDF pp. 8 and 55.

counterexamples.status: Constructed logical scope test; not a historical finding
counterexamples.scenario: Two authors use 'transduction', but one investigates individuation and the other conversion at an organisational boundary.
counterexamples.inference_that_fails: A shared term or useful comparison establishes shared mechanism, equivalence, or historical influence.
counterexamples.reader_check: Read the different questions each source answers; require separate historical evidence for transmission.
counterexamples.basis: The completed 29 October transduction packet, with its source locators and explicit limits. No new full-text reading is claimed here.

counterexamples.status: Constructed editorial stress test; not an empirical case
counterexamples.scenario: A team adds a reflection meeting but its governing assumptions and decisions remain unaltered.
counterexamples.inference_that_fails: Another feedback meeting establishes double-loop learning or a higher Bateson learning level.
counterexamples.reader_check: Find the changed governing assumption or altered process of learning, rather than count meetings or arrows.
counterexamples.basis: The completed 29 October regulation/learning packet. The team is invented and the different classifications remain distinct.

counterexamples.status: Constructed editorial stress test; not an empirical case
counterexamples.scenario: An accurate forecast is attached to an organisation that has no specified response mapping or outcome criterion.
counterexamples.inference_that_fails: Possessing a model or prediction establishes the good-regulator theorem’s assumptions or organisational optimality.
counterexamples.reader_check: State the outcome criterion and regulatory mapping before invoking the theorem.
counterexamples.basis: The completed 29 October primary-source packet, Conant and Ashby electronic PDF pp. 5–9. No new theorem proof is claimed.

reader_route.title: What changes when you follow this line?
steps: Read both endpoint definitions, not just their names.
Identify the unit of analysis and the sense of the shared term.
Read the source locator, scope, and recorded review status.
Try the named counterexample before transferring the claim to a service or institution.
Keep an editorial comparison separate from historical influence or demonstrated effectiveness.
reader_route.autonomy_note: Follow the contrast between self-production of a unity and operational discretion within a wider organisation. Neither question settles the other.
